events.speaker: LOUISA
events.text: The post I was promised is in a town that never got built. The books are real enough. Forty of them came off the wagon into the mud and I have dried every one. Somebody out here wants reading. I am not particular which somebody.

events.speaker: LOUISA
events.text: He read his own letter out loud, badly, the whole way to the end, and not one man laughed at him. My sister Adaeze is still waiting on a letter from me. She will hear about this one first.

events.speaker: LOUISA
events.text: A place, then, and half an hour of an evening when the hands will sit still for it. That is the whole of what I am asking. Cordelia Sinclair hauls a library about in a wagon, so plainly the thing can be done.

events.speaker: LOUISA
events.text: You said it wrong at supper on purpose so that I would correct you, and then you sat there pleased with yourself. That was not fair play. I have thought about it a great deal more than I mean to admit.
